title: Baicalin Alleviates Chronic Pancreatitis Fibrosis and Islet Dysfunction via Targeting IFNAR-Mediated JAK/STAT Signaling and Immune Modulation.
authors: Dou, Hehe; Tao, Rui; Yue, Kan; Cheng, Feng; Xu, Zhipeng; Wang, Zhenjie; Zheng, Chuanming
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药黄芩苷通过IFNAR/JAK/STAT信号通路缓解慢性胰腺炎纤维化，核心是蛋白-蛋白信号传导与免疫调节，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，且方法仅含分子对接与转录组分析，无AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is characterized by progressive fibrosis and islet dysfunction, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study elucidates the mechanism by which baicalin ameliorates CP progression through modulation of the interferon-alpha/beta receptor (IFNAR)/janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signaling pathway. In a caerulein-induced CP rat model, baicalin treatment (100 mg/kg/day, 6 weeks) markedly reduced pancreatic injury, collagen deposition, and alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA) expression, alongside decreased serum levels of IL-6, TNF-alpha, TGF-beta, amylase, and lipase. Flow cytometry revealed that baicalin suppressed pancreatic infiltration of CD8(+) T cells, macrophages, and NK cells while elevating regulatory T (Treg) cell proportions. Transcriptomic analysis identified JAK/STAT signaling as a key pathway inhibited by baicalin, with molecular docking confirming its direct binding to IFNAR. In vitro, baicalin (10 muM) attenuated TGF-beta1-activated pancreatic stellate cell (PSC) activation, evidenced by reduced lipid droplet loss and alpha-SMA/COL1A1 expression. Overexpression of IFNAR reversed baicalin's anti-fibrotic effects, whereas co-treatment with the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib partially restored its efficacy. In vivo, IFNAR overexpression diminished baicalin's therapeutic benefits, but ruxolitinib co-administration mitigated pancreatic damage. These findings demonstrate that baicalin alleviates CP fibrosis and islet dysfunction by targeting IFNAR to suppress JAK/STAT signaling, modulating immune cell dynamics, and inhibiting PSC activation. This study highlights IFNAR as a novel therapeutic target and positions baicalin as a promising candidate for CP treatment.
abstract_zh: 慢性胰腺炎（CP）以进行性纤维化和胰岛功能障碍为特征，然而有效的治疗策略仍然有限。本研究阐明了黄芩苷通过调节干扰素-α/β受体（IFNAR）/Janus激酶（JAK）/信号转导与转录激活因子（STAT）信号通路改善CP进展的机制。在雨蛙素诱导的CP大鼠模型中，黄芩苷治疗（100 mg/kg/天，6周）显著减轻了胰腺损伤、胶原沉积和α-平滑肌肌动蛋白（alpha-SMA）表达，同时降低了血清中IL-6、TNF-alpha、TGF-beta、淀粉酶和脂肪酶的水平。流式细胞术显示，黄芩苷抑制了胰腺中CD8(+) T细胞、巨噬细胞和NK细胞的浸润，同时提高了调节性T（Treg）细胞的比例。转录组分析确定JAK/STAT信号是黄芩苷抑制的关键通路，分子对接证实其直接结合IFNAR。在体外，黄芩苷（10 μM）减弱了TGF-beta1激活的胰腺星状细胞（PSC）活化，表现为脂滴丢失减少以及alpha-SMA/COL1A1表达降低。IFNAR过表达逆转了黄芩苷的抗纤维化作用，而与JAK抑制剂鲁索替尼联合处理则部分恢复其疗效。在体内，IFNAR过表达削弱了黄芩苷的治疗益处，但鲁索替尼联合给药减轻了胰腺损伤。这些发现表明，黄芩苷通过靶向IFNAR抑制JAK/STAT信号、调节免疫细胞动态并抑制PSC活化，从而缓解CP纤维化和胰岛功能障碍。本研究突出IFNAR作为新型治疗靶点，并将黄芩苷定位为CP治疗的有前景候选药物。
